messages:
From: Carlos Rios <c.rios@odyssey.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate & tail latency on /generate - urgent

Marissa,

Quick heads up — starting ~08:45 PT we've seen a sustained increase in 5xxs and tail latency on our /generate endpoint. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 3.8% and 99th percentile latency is spiking above 5s. This is impacting our real-time assistant flow and several customers are reporting degraded UX.

Attached: odyssey_trace_0711.log (sample traces), plus we can share internal dashboards if helpful. We've already rerouted some traffic to degraded cached flows but that's a temporary mitigation.

Can you confirm this has been received and whether Redwood has a recommended mitigation path (model fallback, routing to lower-latency variant, or temporary rate limiting)? We need a customer-facing timeline — our executive team is asking for an ETA.

—Carlos
Director of Engineering, Odyssey.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Rios <c.rios@odyssey.ai>

Subject: Re: High error rate & tail latency on /generate - urgent

Carlos — thanks for the flag and the trace. I’ve looped in SRE (Karthik), Customer Success (Lauren), and Sales leadership (Aditya). We’re designating this as a Priority P1 and opening an executive liaison channel.

Immediate plan:
- Karthik / SRE: please run a top-level triage and confirm whether this is model-level, infra, or routing. Prioritize rollback/variant routing if safe.
- Lauren / CS: I’ll draft a short status note to Odyssey execs after we confirm the root cause. Keep me posted on customer impact signals.
- Aditya: please flag any commercial asks (credits / SLA exceptions) you want prioritized.

Carlos — I’ll send a consolidated update to your team within 90 minutes. For now, please continue to share traces and any spike correlation (region, model version, request size).

- Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Carlos Rios <c.rios@odyssey.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate & tail latency on /generate - urgent

Marissa / Carlos — triage notes so far (initial 20m):
- Symptom: sudden increase in model-side OOM/retry cycles affecting a subset of 8k-12k token requests. Error payloads show repeated kernel memalloc failures followed by 502/504.
- Scope: primarily US-west region, model: gptx-large-v2@rev-2028-06-29, affects ~22% of Odyssey traffic to /generate (confirmed by sampling).
- Immediate mitigations we are applying now:
  1) Auto-fallback: routing 40% of new traffic to gptx-large-v2-quant (lower memory) for Odyssey customer routes. This should reduce OOMs within ~2 minutes of rollout.
  2) Prefix caching enabled for common prompt templates (reduces KV pressure).
  3) Throttling enforcement for requests >8k tokens for affected routes.
- Expected near-term effect: we expect error rate to fall toward baseline within 10–20 minutes as fallback warms. 99th percentile latency should improve but may remain elevated for longer as KV caches rehydrate.

Diagnostics and next steps:
- Collected extended traces (attached odyssey_trace_0711.log) and started a targeted heap sampling on the GPU pool serving Odyssey dedicated instances.
- If fallback does not stabilize within 30 minutes we’ll consider a hot-patch to the scheduler (config tweak) and engage kernel-level team.

I’ll update with metrics from the rollout at +15 and +30 minutes.

—Karthik
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

--- Draft status note to Odyssey leadership ---
Subject: Status update — /generate incident (Jul 11)
Estimated impact: Some requests to /generate experienced elevated error rates (~3–4%) and increased tail latency, primarily in US-west, since ~08:45 PT.
What we’ve done: Redwood has routed a subset of traffic to a lower-memory model variant, enabled prefix caching, and throttled extremely large requests. Initial mitigation has already reduced error rates in sampled routes; we’re monitoring for full recovery.
ETA: We expect stabilization within 30–60 minutes; full latency normalization may take up to 3 hours while caches rehydrate.
Customer remedy: We are proposing a one-time usage credit and an SLA credit for the impacted service window. Draft proposal attached (sla_credit_proposal_v1.pdf).
Next steps: We will provide a post-incident summary and detailed root cause analysis within 48 hours.

--- end draft ---

Marissa / Aditya — what do you want for the public-facing ETA and the proposed credit SKU?

—Lauren
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Rios <c.rios@odyssey.ai>, Odyssey Ops <support@odyssey.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Customer update — /generate stabilization in progress (Jul 11)

Carlos — updating you with what we’ve confirmed and the actions we’re taking.

Summary (what happened):
- Root cause (prelim): model memory pressure on gptx-large-v2@rev-2028-06-29 causing intermittent kernel allocation failures under specific long-request workloads.
- Scope: primarily impacted Odyssey traffic in US-west; ~22% of requests to /generate saw elevated errors during the window starting ~08:45 PT.

What we did (now):
- Routed 40% of traffic to gptx-large-v2-quant (lower-memory variant) — error rate dropped from ~3.8% to ~0.6% in sampled routes.
- Enabled aggressive prefix/KV caching for your top templates (reduced repeated mem pressure).
- Enforced temporary token-size throttling for requests >8k tokens.

Customer commitments and remedies:
- Near-term: stabilization is in progress; we expect full service normalization within 90 minutes from now (by ~15:15 PT) barring unexpected regressions.
- Credits: Redwood proposes a one-time usage credit equivalent to estimated excess error-impacted tokens and a partial SLA credit for the window. Draft attached: sla_credit_proposal_v1.pdf. We can finalize numbers with your team.
- Post-incident: we will deliver a full RCA and remediation plan (kernel and scheduler fixes + improved model variant routing) within 48 hours and schedule a follow-up technical review.

Operational links and artifacts:
- Live metrics: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ods/OD-4852/latency?range=1h
- Runbook & traces: https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/OD-4852/runbook-0711.md
- Attached: odyssey_trace_0711.log, slo-impact-summary-0711.xlsx, sla_credit_proposal_v1.pdf

If you need an executive-level bridge, we can arrange a 11:30 PT sync with our CTO and your Head of Eng. Otherwise I’ll send a brief post-mortem within 48 hours.

Thanks for the quick signals here — please reply with any additional impact details and whether you want the executive sync.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
